Criminal Law Practice Guide

What Documents to Prepare When Consulting a Criminal Defence Lawyer in Nepal

📅 Published: 2025-03-10
🔄 Updated: 2025-10-01
⏱ 6 min read
🔍 Review: Senior Advocate Lead Counsel, Supreme Court Bar Association
Direct Legal Answer & Overview

When consulting a criminal defence advocate in Nepal, family members or the accused should prepare: 1) The official copy of the Arrest Notice (Pakrau Purji) or Search Warrant; 2) The FIR number and copy of the First Information Report (Jaheri Darkhwast); 3) The name of the police post and investigating officer; 4) Proof of medical condition or pre-existing illnesses; 5) Documentary alibi evidence (CCTV footage, travel tickets, time-stamped mobile logs); and 6) Identity documents of family members prepared to stand as bail guarantors (Jamanatdars).

Key Practical Takeaways

  • Time is critical in criminal matters; provide the exact date, time, and location of detention immediately.
  • Gather alibi documentation before digital server logs or CCTV recordings are overwritten.
  • Prepare identity and land ownership documents for prospective bail surety.

In a criminal matter, hours and minutes matter. When a family member or corporate executive is detained by police in Nepal, arriving at your defence advocate's office with clear factual records enables immediate counsel intervention, protection against unlawful questioning, and swift bail preparation.

1. Exact Details of Police Detention

Bring precise details: What specific police division executed the arrest (e.g. Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office, Metropolitan Police Circle Teku, or District Police Office Sunsari)? What is the full name and rank of the Investigating Officer (Anusandhan Adhikrit)?

2. The Arrest Slip & FIR Details

Under Section 9 of the Muluki Criminal Procedure Code 2074, police must provide an arrest memo (Pakrau Purji). Obtain this document from the police post. Note the exact FIR (Jaheri) number and date of registration.

3. Alibi and Digital Evidence Preservation

If the accused was elsewhere when the alleged offense occurred, speed is paramount. Many private commercial CCTV systems overwrite footage within 7 to 15 days. Bring travel tickets, toll receipts, hotel registers, or phone GPS location summaries so your advocate can formally petition the court or police to preserve this objective evidence.

Statutory Citations & Governing Nepal Legislation

Statute / Act Section / Rule Legal Significance
Muluki Criminal Procedure Code 2074 Section 9 & 10 Requirement for police to provide written arrest slips to detainee or family.

Documentary Checklist for this Procedure

  • ✔ Arrest Notice (Pakrau Purji) or summons notice copy
  • ✔ First Information Report (FIR / Jaheri) copy if available
  • ✔ Medical prescriptions or hospital cards of detainee
  • ✔ Alibi documentation (travel receipts, tickets, digital communications)

Frequently Asked Questions on this Topic

Can a lawyer visit a detainee in police custody on weekends or holidays in Nepal?

Yes. Under the Constitution of Nepal, access to legal counsel is an absolute fundamental right that applies 24/7, including weekends, Saturdays, and public holidays.
